text:
Nina (Billing): Quick alert — saw 63 Stripe invoices posted to NetSuite with wrong tax codes; customers in UK got US tax treatment. Started after domain-hint scrub we rolled Friday.

Oscar (Engineered Billing): Confirmed. The normalizer removed subdomain components (eg sales.uk.acme.com -> acme.com) causing resolver to pick wrong customer record. Fuzzy match favored US record when domain collision existed.

Maya (Finance): This affects VAT reporting. Close in 8 days. We need a safe remediation that preserves audit trail.

Ken (SRE): Any DLQ or replay evidence? AuditBot shows 1 DLQ message (dlq_99) but most were processed normally.

Oscar (Engineered Billing): I'll run a dry-run to enumerate affected invoices and include amount, currency, original_ns_id, expected_ns_subsidiary, suggested_action (credit+recreate|journal). Will post CSV to #finance-private in 6h.

Maya (Finance): Prefer credit+recreate to maintain clear audit trail. Include GL impact and list of invoices already settled.

Ken (SRE): Suggest pausing monthly export and scheduling corrective run in low-traffic window Sunday 02:00 UTC. We'll also add a cache whitelist to preserve corporate subdomains.

AuditBot: Reminder: snapshot export scheduled Wed 06:00 UTC.

Nina (Billing): Thanks — proceed with dry-run. Tag any corrected NS invoices with redwood:correction:2026-03-28.
